title: The controller lock is a kernel flock on a file that is never deleted
objective: At most one process can hold `osx.PidLock` on a lock file, because holding it means holding an exclusive flock on that file, which stays in place (emptied) after release.
outline: devloop/core/osx.py `class PidLock` (about 40 lines today): replace the `O_EXCL` create / JSON write / unlink body with the flock pattern of core/ticketlock.py `take()` (open `O_RDWR | O_CREAT`, `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`, `BlockingIOError` means held). On held: read the stamp with `read_json` for the message (an empty or broken file gives no stamp; then say the holder has not written its stamp yet), close the fd, raise. On taken: read the stamp; a live one (not `stamp_dead`) refuses per B5 (close the fd first); else `os.ftruncate(fd, 0)`, write `json.dumps(stamp())` at offset 0, `os.fsync(fd)`, keep the fd, `held = True`. `release()`: when held, `os.ftruncate(fd, 0)`, close the fd, `held = False`; idempotent. `import fcntl` at the top of osx.py. The one caller is ticket_controller.py `main()` (unchanged). devloop/board.py `controller_alive()` stays as it is (an empty file reads as no lock). devloop/README.md: one sentence next to the existing `controller.lock` sentence in the service section (T159Acceptance reads that section for `controller.lock` and `exit 0`; keep both and add no absolute home path). Measured on HEAD 4797416: an empty lock file is taken over, release deletes the file, a live stamp refuses with `already running (pid ...`. Out of scope: making controller_alive() test the flock; any other lock file.

An addCleanup closes the child's stdin and waits for it whatever happens. Red today: the first acquire succeeds (measured). This ticket is about holding processes, so those words are close: nothing here needs to end a process from outside - let holder children end by closing their stdin, and write none of those words anywhere, comments included (say 'stop' or 'end').
acceptance: B1 While another process holds an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on the lock file, `osx.PidLock(path).acquire()` raises `osx.OSFailure` whose text contains `already running` and the lock path, and leaves the file untouched (same size and content, not deleted); this holds also when the file is empty, as it is between a holder's open and its stamp write. Today an empty lock file is taken over (measured 2026-11-28: acquire succeeds and writes its own stamp).
B2 Once that holder has exited (and been reaped), `acquire()` succeeds and the file then holds this process's stamp: `osx.read_json(path)["pid"] == os.getpid()`.

B3 `release()` leaves the lock file in place with 0 bytes (the stamp cleared), so `board.controller_alive(cfg)` for a config whose `worktree_root` holds that `controller.lock` is False; a second `release()` raises nothing. Today release deletes the file (measured).

B4 How the lock is held (the rule of core/slots.py and core/ticketlock.py): `acquire` opens the path with `os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT`, takes `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` on that fd and keeps the fd open while held, and writes the stamp into the same file in place (truncate to 0, write the JSON, fsync) - never through `atomic_write`, `os.replace` or an unlink, because a lock on a replaced file stops counting. The fd is not inheritable (the `os.open` default), so issuers, regressions and fixers the controller starts never hold the lock. `release()` truncates the file to 0 bytes, then closes the fd (which drops the flock). An OSError other than 'held by another' becomes an `osx.OSFailure` naming the path.

B5 Kept: after the flock is taken, a stamp already in the file whose process is alive (a controller started before this change holds no flock) still refuses with the existing `already running (pid <pid> on <host> since <started>); lock <path>` text, and the flock is let go again; a stamp whose process is dead is taken over; a second `PidLock` on the same path in the same process while the first holds is refused (a separate open file description).

B6 `board.controller_alive()` is unchanged and its existing tests (test_board_dag.py `test_dep_satisfied_and_controller_alive`, `LiveIdleReasonUnits`, the lock fixtures in test_live.py) pass unchanged; `ticket_controller.main` still takes the lock with `osx.PidLock(...).acquire()` and releases it in its `finally`.

B7 The PidLock docstring and devloop/README.md (next to the sentence about stopping a manually started controller by the pid in `<worktrees>/controller.lock`) say that the file stays after the controller stops, emptied, and that the lock is a flock on it.

4.1 Acceptance results must be honest.
- Problem (read in code): a skipped acceptance case (rc 0) counts as green; `red_check()` treats skip as red but
  expectedFailure is recorded as `pass`; nothing checks whether the worker edited the `T<N>Acceptance` cases.
- Layer 1: `run_cases()` requires each case to be exactly `pass`; `red_check()` requires exactly `fail`.
  expectedFailure is recorded as `xfail` (not pass).
- Layer 2: from round 2 on, a worker change that alters the `T<N>Acceptance` definitions is sent back. Compare by
  AST (classes and functions), and check the count of same-named definitions. A round that went through `--revise`
  (the ticket was rewritten) is not a violation. The verifier prompt gets one line: helpers specific to this ticket
  go inside the class.

4.2 Controller lock uses flock.
- Problem (read in code): `PidLock` creates an empty file and then writes JSON; two `actl run` starting at once can
  both take the lock.
- Do: keep the lock file (do not delete it), use `fcntl.flock`, clear the stamp on release; `controller_alive()` and
  existing tests keep passing.

4.3 start_fixer writes once.
- Do: `start_fixer()` writes the pool once, after the spawn, and passes `--round` to `auto_fixer.py`.
